meta.documentTitle: Mahabharat Episode 4: Shakuntala and the Birth of Bharata

header.title: Mahabharat Episode 4: Shakuntala and the Birth of Bharata
header.description: The tale of King Vishwamitra's daughter Shakuntala, her love with King Dushyanta, Sage Durvasa's curse, and the birth of Emperor Bharata—after whom India is named Bharatvarsh.

intro.title: From King to Sage
leads: Generations after Puru, King Vishwamitra (also known as Kaushika) realized that a king's power was tiny compared to the spiritual power of rishis and sages.

Determined to become a sage himself, Vishwamitra retreated into the deep forest to perform intense austerities. Seeing his fierce dedication, Indra felt threatened that his supreme position in heaven might be taken.
To disrupt his spiritual power, Indra sent the celestial apsara Menaka to distract Vishwamitra. She succeeded in seducing him, and from their union, a girl child was born.

storyElements.html: Realizing that his hard-earned spiritual power was lost to distraction, Vishwamitra flew into a rage and walked away, abandoning both mother and child.
Menaka, being a celestial visitor with limited time on Earth, could not stay to raise the baby. She left the infant girl on the banks of the Malini River and returned to heaven.
Local Shakun birds noticed the helpless infant and shielded her from dangerous predators.
When Sage Kanva passed by and saw birds protecting a human baby, he brought her to his ashram and named her Shakuntala, after the birds that saved her.
Years later, King Dushyanta went hunting in the forest to feed his army. He shot a large stag with an arrow, but the wounded animal fled.
Tracking the stag, Dushyanta found it being gently nursed by Shakuntala, who had raised it as her pet.
Captivated by her grace and compassion, Dushyanta fell in love with her. With Sage Kanva’s approval, they were married in the forest.

bubble.text: I must return to my kingdom to prepare for your arrival. Wear this ring as a token of my love and our marriage. I will return for you soon.

storyElements.html: He placed his royal signet ring on her finger—though, being made for a king, it was too large for her hand.
After Dushyanta left, Shakuntala spent her days lost in continuous daydreaming about her new life as a queen.
One day, the notoriously hot-tempered Sage Durvasa visited the ashram. Shakuntala was so deep in thought that she failed to acknowledge his arrival.

bubble.text: You ignore me! Whoever is holding your attention right now, may he forget you forever!

storyElements.html: Shakuntala snapped back to reality in tears. The people of the ashram explained her marriage to Durvasa and begged for forgiveness.

bubble.text: A curse cannot be recalled, but I will modify it: the moment you show him something that reminds him of you, his memory will return.

storyElements.html: Dushyanta never returned. In time, Shakuntala gave birth to a brave boy named Bharata.
Eventually, Sage Kanva advised her to take her son to the capital so he could know his father.
While crossing a river by boat, Shakuntala dipped her hand in the water, and the oversized royal ring slipped into the river unnoticed.
When she arrived at court, Dushyanta looked at her with complete blankness.

bubble.text: Who are you? How dare you enter my court and claim to be my wife?

storyElements.html: Devastated and humiliated, Shakuntala retreated into the deep wilderness behind the ashram to raise Bharata alone.

storyElements.text: The Birth of a Nation's Name

storyElements.html: Bharata grew up in the wilderness, fearlessly wrestling lions and riding elephants.
Years later, a fisherman found the lost ring inside a fish, and upon seeing it, Dushyanta's memory instantly returned. Grief-stricken, he searched the forests for his lost family.
He stumbled upon a young boy playing fearlessly with full-grown wild lions.

bubble.text: Who are you? Are you a god or a superhuman being?
No, I am Bharata, the son of Dushyanta.

storyElements.html: Sage Kanva arrived to explain the truth, and a tearful Dushyanta reunited with Shakuntala and Bharata, bringing them home to the palace.
Bharata grew into an ideal emperor of vast nobility and strength. It is in honor of his exceptional qualities that the entire nation came to be known as Bharat or Bharatvarsh.
From the line of Emperor Bharata, the ancient history of the Lunar Dynasty continues down to the generations of the Kurus...
